page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4n family. It features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates with dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants. It does not include graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-standard-24-lssd balances compute power and memory capacity within a dedicated hardware class. The vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions it near the standard general-purpose threshold, though it belongs to a compute-centric family. A notable tradeoff is the lack of bundled local storage, as the local storage size is designated as None, requiring external block storage attachment for persistent data.

This server configuration is suitable for workloads requiring dedicated x86_64 compute resources with moderate memory requirements. Applicable use cases include web serving, application servers, containerized microservices, build systems, and distributed compute nodes where local high-speed storage or GPU acceleration is not required.
